speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you haven't provided the infant's history yet. Could you please describe when these episodes of stridor and wheezing occur, and what triggers them? Also, has anyone noticed if they choke on saliva or have trouble breathing while feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the stridor been present since birth, and do these episodes occur specifically when the child looks down or turns his head to the side? REQUEST TEST: Barium_Swallow; REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Barium_Swallow Findings: Compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring. Neck_Ultrasound: Not requested or available in current data.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis is incorrect for an infant; those symptoms instead strongly suggest a structural issue in the larynx or trachea. REQUEST TEST: Flexible_Laryngoscopy to directly visualize the airway during an episode. Please also confirm if you have noticed a "seal-like" barking cough or any "barking" sound when he cries.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Flexible_Laryngoscopy: Not available in current data. Seal-like barking cough: Not observed; wheezing is noted instead.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the absence of a barking cough and the specific exacerbation with neck flexion, I am suspecting a laryngeal web or subglottic stenosis. REQUEST TEST: CT_Neck_with_contrast to evaluate the tracheal diameter and identify any extrinsic compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Laryngeal_Flexibility_Videos. Can you confirm if the child has any difficulty swallowing liquids or solids?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT_Neck_with_contrast Findings: Evidence of tracheal compression and a vascular ring suggestive of a double aortic arch. Laryngeal_Flexibility_Videos: Not available in current data. Difficulty swallowing liquids or solids: Vomiting after feeding is reported, but no specific dysphagia to liquids or solids is documented in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch causing tracheoesophageal compression.
